newsitem.title: CANADA: Oil and gas drilling booms in western Canada.
newsitem.headline: Oil and gas drilling booms in western Canada.

text.p: Early frigid weather and high oil and gas prices sent the number of rigs drilling in western Canada soaring above 400 about two months before the plateau was reached in last year's drilling season.
In its weekly tally, the Canadian Association of Oilwell Drilling Contractors reported that 403 rigs were drilling in the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin, up from 380 last week and 281 last year.
The total number of rigs drilling did not climb above 400 until January 1996 during the last season. The last time the number was above 400 was in mid-March.

In another indication of the current health of Canada's energy sector, CAODC president Don Herring said his group expected the number to remain at least as high as the current level until spring, with the exception of the usual dropoff during the Christmas holiday.
"Certainly the demand that's coming back to us in terms of anecdotal information suggests that it will stay very high," he said.
Producer demand for rigs for shallow gas and heavy oil targets in Alberta and Saskatchewan has created a waiting list for services and begun to stretch drilling staffs at various companies, he said.
Herring said companies had yet to rush into contracting the services of the largest long-range rigs that usually target deep natural gas in the foothills of Alberta and British Columbia.
This week, Alberta had 12 additional rigs drilling compared to last week. Saskatchewan's count grew by 14 and B.C.'s by seven. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
